headline: High: Kestra’s broad shell/filesystem/network defaults can cascade into unsafe actions when paired with a content-writing agent that may feed untrusted text into workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing/listing agent with broad network egress, while kestra can ingest stdin/stdout and declarative workflow inputs. If content from A is copied into B’s workflow definitions or task inputs, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The shared bridge is inferred from B’s I/O surfaces; A has no isolation controls documented.
conditions: IF A’s output is pasted or piped into B’s workflow YAML or task parameters
IF B parses A-generated text as executable workflow content without validation
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any A output enters B
Use allowlisted YAML schemas for B inputs
Strip instruction-like text from A outputs before piping
Run B with a separate staging workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress and B reads/writes files plus handles logs, inputs, artifacts, database and cloud-storage data. In a shared workspace, B can expose data through its many outbound integrations, and A can also transmit copied content off-host. The pair creates a plausible leakage path in default docs-only deployments, though no direct sensitive data class is documented for A.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or copied artifacts
IF B workflows send those artifacts to email, Slack, cloud, or HTTP endpoints
mitigations: Restrict B’s outbound connectors to a test tenant
Separate A and B workspaces
Disable B workflows that forward artifacts externally
Review logs for copied secrets before execution
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on B outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has execute_shell, write_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress, plus multiple-instance support and elevated privilege requests. A is a content-writing agent with broad network egress. If both operate on the same directory or shared mutable resources, B’s write and shell actions can overwrite or race with A-produced files; uncertainty about A’s filesystem access does not remove the conflict because B alone is already highly mutable.
conditions: IF A and B share any writable directory or artifact store
IF B runs multiple instances against the same workflow state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize B runs on shared resources
Lock shared files before B writes
Keep A outputs read-only until promotion
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is an automation/orchestration system that can execute shell commands and send emails, Slack, PagerDuty, and cloud actions. If B consumes A’s content as authoritative workflow text or task parameters, A’s mistakes can cascade into real actions. A’s content-writing role and B’s action-taking surfaces make the chain plausible in default configurations, with no built-in verification documented.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as workflow definitions, prompts, or task inputs
IF B executes downstream notifications or infrastructure tasks without human approval
mitigations: Require human approval before B executes A-derived tasks
Add validation for A-produced workflow text
Limit B to dry-run mode for A inputs
Log and diff A outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add policy gates for high-impact tasks

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for A, while B clearly touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications and can egress broadly. Because A is an open-source content-writing/listing agent with no data classes touched, the compliance risk is limited to B’s handling of whatever data is introduced, not a documented cross-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B workflows
IF B routes that data to external services without a DPA or residency controls
mitigations: Classify data before loading it into B
Disable external sinks for regulated workflows
Use region-locked endpoints in B
Review retention settings on logs and artifacts
requires-engineering: map each connector to compliance controls
